```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# =============================================================================
# HOW THIS FILE IS ORGANIZED
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# This R Markdown file recreates the tables and figures of the paper, starting
# with main-text Table 3 and Figure 1 and then going through the Supplemental
# Material in the order in which it is presented. Each section is a heading
# (what is being produced) followed by one code chunk that produces it.
#
# The first few chunks (setup, helper functions, and "fit all models") produce
# no output; they prepare what the later chunks need.
#
# HOW TO RUN: put this file in the same folder as CTQ_RL_data.csv and knit it
# (e.g., in RStudio, click "Knit"). All paths are relative to this file's folder.
# Knitting takes several minutes because many mixed models are fit.
#
# NOT REPRODUCED HERE:
#   - Supplemental Table 4 (model recovery) and Supplemental Figure 2 (model
#     simulations) require running the Stan models; code available upon request.
# =============================================================================

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center")

library(lme4)          # mixed-effects (multilevel) models
library(lmerTest)      # Satterthwaite p-values for lme4 models
library(interactions)  # Johnson-Neyman intervals
library(MuMIn)         # R-squared for mixed models (r.squaredGLMM)
library(MASS)          # mvrnorm(): Monte Carlo draws for Supplemental Table 16
library(ggplot2)       # figures
library(patchwork)     # combining several ggplots into one figure
library(parallel)      # running the leave-one-participant-out refits in parallel

# Number of cores for the leave-one-participant-out refits (Supplemental
# Table 15). mclapply() cannot run in parallel on Windows, so use 1 core there.
n_cores <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") 1 else max(1, min(4, detectCores() - 1))
```

```{r load-data}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DATA. One row per participant per study wave (see README.txt for a dictionary
# of every variable). Learning parameters are the posterior means from the
# PoP-ORL model (already fit); CTQ and covariates are already merged in.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- read.csv("CTQ_RL_data.csv")

# Last-block traditional scores are the primary version used in the paper;
# the full-task versions (good_proportion, bad_proportion, net_good_bad) are
# used only in Supplemental Tables 8 and 11.

# The eight learning metrics ("outcomes") analyzed in the paper, in paper order.
# name = variable in the data file, value = label used in the tables.
outcomes <- c(
  good_proportion_LastBlock = "Good Deck Proportion (Last Block)",
  bad_proportion_LastBlock  = "Bad Deck Proportion (Last Block)",
  net_good_bad_LastBlock    = "Net Performance (Good Proportion – Bad Proportion) (Last Block)",
  betaB                     = "Go Bias (βb)",
  Arew_qnormed              = "Reward Learning Rate (Arew)",
  Apun_qnormed              = "Punishment Learning Rate (Apun)",
  Overall_A                 = "Averaged Single Learning Rate ((Arew + Apun)/2)",
  betaF                     = "Win/Loss Frequency Sensitivity (βf)")

# The same three traditional metrics computed from ALL trials (Supp. Tables 8, 11)
fulltask_outcomes <- c(
  good_proportion = "Good Deck Proportion (full task)",
  bad_proportion  = "Bad Deck Proportion (full task)",
  net_good_bad    = "Net Performance (full task)")

# Shorter labels used in the summary tables (Table 3, Supp. Tables 10 and 11)
short_label <- c(
  good_proportion_LastBlock = "Good Deck Proportion (last block)",
  bad_proportion_LastBlock  = "Bad Deck Proportion (last block)",
  net_good_bad_LastBlock    = "Net Performance (last block)",
  betaB = "Go Bias (βb)", Arew_qnormed = "Reward Learning Rate (Arew)",
  Apun_qnormed = "Punishment Learning Rate (Apun)",
  Overall_A = "Averaged Single Learning Rate ((Arew + Apun)/2)",
  betaF = "Win/Loss Frequency Sensitivity (βf)",
  good_proportion = "Good Deck Proportion (full task)",
  bad_proportion  = "Bad Deck Proportion (full task)",
  net_good_bad    = "Net Performance (full task)")

# The seven CTQ adversity predictors: two composites and five subscales.
#   centered = mean-centered score used in the models
#   raw      = raw CTQ score (5-25 per subscale), used to report J-N intervals
predictors <- data.frame(
  key      = c("A", "N", "EA", "PA", "SA", "EN", "PN"),
  title    = c("Abuse Composite", "Neglect Composite", "Emotional Abuse (EA)", "Physical Abuse (PA)",
               "Sexual Abuse (SA)", "Emotional Neglect (EN)", "Physical Neglect (PN)"),
  name     = c("Abuse Composite", "Neglect Composite", "Emotional Abuse", "Physical Abuse",
               "Sexual Abuse", "Emotional Neglect", "Physical Neglect"),
  abbr     = c("Abuse Composite", "Neglect Composite", "EA", "PA", "SA", "EN", "PN"),
  centered = paste0("ctq_", c("A", "N", "EA", "PA", "SA", "EN", "PN"), "_T1_c"),
  raw      = paste0("ctq_", c("A", "N", "EA", "PA", "SA", "EN", "PN"), "_T1_avg"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
rownames(predictors) <- predictors$key
subscales <- c("EA", "PA", "SA", "EN", "PN")

# Covariates in Models 3 and 4 and the random-effects structure of every model:
# a random intercept and a random age slope for each participant.
covariates <- "NonVerbal_Std_centered + child_sex + eprime"
random_fx  <- "(1 | id) + (0 + age_centered | id)"
```

```{r helper-functions}
# =============================================================================
# HELPER FUNCTIONS (no output)
# =============================================================================

# --- Formatting --------------------------------------------------------------
# Number with 3 decimals and no leading zero (e.g., -0.045 -> "-.045")
f3 <- function(x, digits = 3) sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
# Number with 2 decimals and no leading zero
f2 <- function(x) f3(x, 2)
# p-value: "<.001" or three decimals with no leading zero
fp <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p < .001, "<.001", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p))))
# Significance stars from a p-value
stars <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "", ifelse(p < .001, "***", ifelse(p < .01, "**", ifelse(p < .05, "*", ""))))
# Estimate, stars, and 95% CI on two lines, e.g., "-.009 **<br>[-.015 – -.003]"
cell_est_ci <- function(est, lo, hi, p, bold = FALSE) {
  s <- stars(p)
  txt <- sprintf("%s%s\n[%s – %s]", f3(est), ifelse(s == "", "", paste0(" ", s)), f3(lo), f3(hi))
  if (bold) txt <- paste0("<b>", gsub("\n", "</b>\n<b>", txt), "</b>")
  txt
}

# --- Showing a data frame as a simple HTML table -----------------------------
show_table <- function(df) {
  # When a chunk is run by itself in RStudio (not knitted), return a plain data
  # frame, which RStudio always shows as a table. (The HTML formatting used for
  # the knitted file is stripped: <b> bold tags removed, line breaks -> spaces.)
  running_alone <- isTRUE(getOption("rstudio.notebook.executing")) || !isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))
  if (running_alone) {
    df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) trimws(gsub("<br>|\\n", " ", gsub("</?b>", "", as.character(x)))))
    return(df)
  }
  # When knitting: an HTML table, with line breaks inside cells
  df[] <- lapply(df, function(x) gsub("\n", "<br>", as.character(x)))
  knitr::kable(df, format = "html", escape = FALSE, row.names = FALSE,
               table.attr = 'class="simple-table"')
}

# --- Fitting one mixed model -------------------------------------------------
# Maximum likelihood (so models can be compared with likelihood-ratio tests).
# If the fit is singular (random-slope variance estimated at ~0), the random age
# slope is dropped and the model is refit with a random intercept only. This is
# expected for some Good Deck Proportion models and is shown in the output as "—"
# in the tau-11 row of the Supplemental Table 9 sub-tables (see its caption).
fit_lmm <- function(formula, data) {
  ctrl <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
  # (suppressMessages hides lme4's "boundary (singular) fit" message; the singular
  # case is handled on purpose just below)
  m <- tryCatch(suppressMessages(lmer(as.formula(formula), data = data, REML = FALSE, control = ctrl)),
                error = function(e) NULL)
  slope_dropped <- FALSE
  if (!is.null(m) && isSingular(m)) {
    f_no_slope <- sub("\\(1 \\| id\\) \\+ \\(0 \\+ age_centered \\| id\\)", "(1 | id)", formula)
    m2 <- tryCatch(suppressMessages(lmer(as.formula(f_no_slope), data = data, REML = FALSE, control = ctrl)),
                   error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(m2)) { m <- m2; slope_dropped <- TRUE }
  }
  list(model = m, slope_dropped = slope_dropped)
}

# --- Unconditional growth: linear (Model 1) vs. quadratic (Model 2) ----------
# Fits both models and compares them with a likelihood-ratio test. The quadratic
# model is kept only if p < .05.
growth_shape <- function(outcome, data) {
  r1 <- fit_lmm(paste(outcome, "~ age_centered +", random_fx), data)
  r2 <- fit_lmm(paste(outcome, "~ age_centered + age_squared +", random_fx), data)
  m2_for_test <- r2$model
  # If Model 1 had to drop its random slope but Model 2 did not, refit Model 2
  # without the slope as well so the two models differ only in the quadratic term.
  if (r1$slope_dropped && !r2$slope_dropped) {
    m2_for_test <- lmer(as.formula(paste(outcome, "~ age_centered + age_squared + (1 | id)")),
                        data = data, REML = FALSE,
                        control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5)))
  }
  lrt <- anova(r1$model, m2_for_test, test = "LRT")
  list(r1 = r1, r2 = r2, lrt = lrt, p_lrt = lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
       use_quadratic = !is.na(lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]) && lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] < .05)
}

# --- The full nested-model sequence (Models 1-4) for one outcome and predictor
#   Model 1: linear growth (age)
#   Model 2: quadratic growth (age + age^2)
#   Model 3: winning growth shape + covariates (IQ, sex, administration mode)
#   Model 4: Model 3 + CTQ predictor + its interaction with age (and with
#            age^2 if the quadratic shape won)  <- the primary model of the paper
# extra_terms: optional extra covariates written as a formula string, used for
#   the specificity and robustness analyses (Supp. Tables 12 and 13).
fit_models <- function(outcome, ctq_var, data, extra_terms = "") {
  gs   <- growth_shape(outcome, data)
  quad <- gs$use_quadratic
  growth <- if (quad) "age_centered + age_squared" else "age_centered"
  M3 <- fit_lmm(paste(outcome, "~", growth, extra_terms, "+", covariates, "+", random_fx), data)
  f4 <- if (quad) {
    paste(outcome, "~ age_centered *", ctq_var, "+ age_squared *", ctq_var, extra_terms,
          "+", covariates, "+", random_fx)
  } else {
    paste(outcome, "~ age_centered *", ctq_var, extra_terms, "+", covariates, "+", random_fx)
  }
  M4 <- fit_lmm(f4, data)
  # The age^2 x CTQ interaction is FDR-corrected across all eight outcomes, so we
  # also need it for outcomes where the linear shape won: fit a quadratic Model 4
  # for every outcome (this is just Model 4 when the quadratic shape already won).
  if (quad) {
    M4_quad <- M4$model
  } else {
    M4_quad <- fit_lmm(paste(outcome, "~ age_centered *", ctq_var, "+ age_squared *", ctq_var,
                             extra_terms, "+", covariates, "+", random_fx), data)$model
  }
  ref <- if (quad) gs$r2$model else gs$r1$model        # the winning unconditional model
  list(outcome = outcome, ctq_var = ctq_var, use_quadratic = quad, growth = gs,
       M1 = gs$r1$model, M2 = gs$r2$model, M3 = M3$model, M4 = M4$model, M4_quad = M4_quad,
       slope_dropped = c(gs$r1$slope_dropped, gs$r2$slope_dropped, M3$slope_dropped, M4$slope_dropped),
       lrt_12   = gs$lrt,
       lrt_ref3 = anova(ref, M3$model, test = "LRT"),   # Model 3 vs. winning unconditional model
       lrt_ref4 = anova(ref, M4$model, test = "LRT"),   # Model 4 vs. winning unconditional model
       lrt_34   = anova(M3$model, M4$model, test = "LRT"))  # Model 4 vs. Model 3
}

# --- Pulling numbers out of fitted models ------------------------------------
# Fixed effects: estimate, 95% Wald CI, and p-value (one row per term)
fixed_effects <- function(model) {
  s <- summary(model)$coefficients
  data.frame(term = rownames(s), est = s[, "Estimate"],
             lo = s[, "Estimate"] - 1.96 * s[, "Std. Error"],
             hi = s[, "Estimate"] + 1.96 * s[, "Std. Error"],
             p = s[, "Pr(>|t|)"], row.names = NULL, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}
# Names of the three CTQ terms in Model 4
ctq_terms <- function(ctq_var) {
  c(baseline = ctq_var,                         # CTQ effect at the centering age
    age      = paste0("age_centered:", ctq_var),   # CTQ x age interaction
    age2     = paste0(ctq_var, ":age_squared"))    # CTQ x age^2 interaction
}
# p-value of a CTQ term from a fit_models() result. The age^2 interaction comes
# from the quadratic Model 4 so that it exists for every outcome.
term_p <- function(fit, which) {
  model <- if (which == "age2") fit$M4_quad else fit$M4
  fe <- fixed_effects(model)
  fe$p[fe$term == ctq_terms(fit$ctq_var)[[which]]]
}
# Random-effect variances, intraclass correlation, and R-squared of a model
random_effects <- function(model, slope_dropped) {
  vc <- VarCorr(model)
  list(sigma2 = sigma(model)^2, tau00 = vc[["id"]][1, 1],
       tau11 = if (slope_dropped) NA else vc[["id.1"]][1, 1])
}
icc <- function(model) { re <- random_effects(model, TRUE); re$tau00 / (re$tau00 + re$sigma2) }
r2  <- function(model) r.squaredGLMM(model)[1, c("R2c", "R2m")]   # conditional and marginal

# --- Johnson-Neyman interval for the age x CTQ interaction -------------------
# Finds the CTQ scores at which the age slope is significantly different from
# zero. Bounds are shifted back to the raw CTQ-score scale. Returns text such as
# "< 5.64; > 9.18" (slope significant below/above these scores).
jn_object <- function(model, ctq_var) {
  # (johnson_neyman() needs the variable names unquoted, hence bquote())
  tryCatch(suppressWarnings(eval(bquote(
    interactions::johnson_neyman(.(model), pred = age_centered, modx = .(as.name(ctq_var)),
                                 alpha = .05, plot = FALSE)))), error = function(e) NULL)
}
ctq_offset <- function(ctq_var) mean(dat[[sub("_c$", "_avg", ctq_var)]], na.rm = TRUE)  # centering constant
jn_text <- function(model, ctq_var) {
  jn <- jn_object(model, ctq_var)
  if (is.null(jn)) return("")
  bounds <- sort(as.numeric(jn$bounds) + ctq_offset(ctq_var))
  if (length(bounds) == 0) return("all observed values")
  if (length(bounds) == 2) {
    b <- sprintf("%.2f", bounds)
    return(if (isTRUE(jn$inside_interval)) paste0(b[1], " – ", b[2]) else paste0("< ", b[1], "; > ", b[2]))
  }
  sprintf("crossover at %.2f", bounds)
}
```

```{r fit-all-models}
# =============================================================================
# FIT ALL MODELS (no output)
# For every CTQ predictor x learning metric, fit Models 1-4. Results are stored
# in fits[[predictor key]][[outcome name]] and reused by the tables below.
# =============================================================================
fits <- list()
for (k in predictors$key) {
  fits[[k]] <- list()
  for (y in names(outcomes)) {
    fits[[k]][[y]] <- fit_models(y, predictors[k, "centered"], dat)
  }
}

# Same models for the three traditional metrics computed from the full task
# (needed for Supplemental Table 11); only the five subscales are analyzed.
fits_full <- list()
for (k in subscales) {
  fits_full[[k]] <- list()
  for (y in names(fulltask_outcomes)) {
    fits_full[[k]][[y]] <- fit_models(y, predictors[k, "centered"], dat)
  }
}

# False discovery rate (Benjamini-Hochberg) correction: for each CTQ predictor
# and each model term (baseline effect, age interaction, age^2 interaction), the
# p-values are corrected across the eight learning metrics. Returns a matrix of
# corrected p-values (rows = the three terms, columns = metrics).
fdr_correct <- function(fit_list, family) {
  q <- sapply(family, function(y) rep(NA_real_, 3))
  rownames(q) <- c("baseline", "age", "age2")
  for (w in rownames(q)) {
    p <- sapply(family, function(y) term_p(fit_list[[y]], w))
    q[w, ] <- p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
  }
  q
}
fdr <- lapply(setNames(predictors$key, predictors$key), function(k) fdr_correct(fits[[k]], names(outcomes)))
# Full-task version: the family of eight is the three full-task traditional
# metrics plus the five model-based metrics.
fdr_full <- lapply(setNames(subscales, subscales), function(k) {
  fl <- c(fits_full[[k]], fits[[k]][names(outcomes)[4:8]])
  fdr_correct(fl, c(names(fulltask_outcomes), names(outcomes)[4:8]))
})
```

```{r summary-table-function}
# =============================================================================
# FUNCTION that builds the "summary" tables (Table 3, Supp. Tables 10 and 11):
# one column per CTQ predictor; for each learning metric, the baseline effect and
# the age (and age^2) interaction as estimate [95% CI]. Stars = uncorrected p
# (* < .05, ** < .01, *** < .001). Bold = survives FDR correction (q < .05).
# A Johnson-Neyman row is added under age interactions that survive FDR correction.
# =============================================================================
summary_table <- function(pred_keys, fit_sets, fdr_sets, metrics) {
  header <- c("", predictors[pred_keys, "title"])
  rows <- list()
  add <- function(...) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <<- c(...)
  for (y in metrics) {
    add(paste0("<b>", short_label[[y]], "</b>"), rep("", length(pred_keys)))
    fs <- lapply(pred_keys, function(k) fit_sets[[k]][[y]])
    one_row <- function(label, which) {
      cells <- mapply(function(f, k) {
        fe <- fixed_effects(if (which == "age2") f$M4_quad else f$M4)
        r <- fe[fe$term == ctq_terms(f$ctq_var)[[which]], ]
        if (nrow(r) == 0) return("")
        cell_est_ci(r$est, r$lo, r$hi, r$p, bold = fdr_sets[[k]][which, y] < .05)
      }, fs, pred_keys)
      add(label, cells)
    }
    one_row("Adversity Baseline Effect", "baseline")
    one_row("Interaction of Adversity × Age", "age")
    # Johnson-Neyman row (only for age interactions that survive FDR correction)
    sig <- sapply(pred_keys, function(k) fdr_sets[[k]]["age", y] < .05)
    if (any(sig)) {
      jn <- mapply(function(f, k, s) {
        if (!s) return("")
        p <- term_p(f, "age")
        paste0(jn_text(f$M4, f$ctq_var), ifelse(stars(p) == "", "", paste0(" ", stars(p))))
      }, fs, pred_keys, sig)
      add("J-N Adversity Levels of Sig", jn)
    }
    # Age^2 interaction row, only shown for metrics whose winning shape is quadratic
    if (any(sapply(fs, function(f) f$use_quadratic))) {
      cells <- mapply(function(f, k) {
        if (!f$use_quadratic) return("")
        fe <- fixed_effects(f$M4)
        r <- fe[fe$term == ctq_terms(f$ctq_var)[["age2"]], ]
        cell_est_ci(r$est, r$lo, r$hi, r$p, bold = fdr_sets[[k]]["age2", y] < .05)
      }, fs, pred_keys)
      add("Interaction of Adversity × Age²", cells)
    }
  }
  df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(df) <- header
  df
}
```

## Table 3 (main text). Effects of Adversity Subtypes on Learning Metric Development

Estimates (unstandardized b) and 95% CIs from Model 4 for each CTQ subscale. Stars show uncorrected p-values; bold shows effects that survive FDR correction. "J-N" rows give the CTQ scores at which the age slope is significant.

```{r table3}
tab3 <- summary_table(subscales, fits, fdr, names(outcomes))
show_table(tab3)
```

## Figure 1 (main text). Effects of Adversity Subtypes on Learning Metric Development Surviving FDR Correction

Same plotting code as the paper's figure. Top: model-predicted trajectories for youth with low (mean − 1 SD) and high (mean + 1 SD) levels of the CTQ subscale, with each participant's data in grey. Bottom: Johnson-Neyman plot of the age-related slope across levels of adversity severity (blue = significant positive slope, grey = not significant, red = significant negative slope; the solid vertical line marks the moderate-severity cutoff; dashed vertical lines mark the boundaries of the region of significance), with an arrow showing low to high adversity. (A) Emotional abuse and Punishment Learning Rate. (B) Physical abuse and Go Bias. (C) Physical abuse and Good Deck Proportion (last block).

xbar_green   <- col_low_sig    # low-adversity end
xbar_orange  <- col_high_sig   # high-adversity end
xbar_neutral <- "#E6E2DA"      # most-neutral tone at the cutoff line

xbar_neutral_halfwidth <- 1.0

xbar_arrow_frac <- 0.04

TITLE_SZ         <- 11         # overall combined-plot title
SUBPLOT_TITLE_SZ <- 9.5        # per-panel subtitles
AXIS_TITLE_SZ    <- 10         # x-axis titles
Y_AXIS_TITLE_SZ  <- 10         # y-axis titles
AXIS_TEXT_SZ     <- 8          # tick labels
SUBPLOT_SUB_SZ   <- AXIS_TEXT_SZ  # p-value sub-line — TIED to Y-axis text

panel_font  <- if ("Helvetica Neue" %in% systemfonts::system_fonts()$family) "Helvetica Neue" else "sans"

strip_lead0 <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  v <- ifelse(is.na(x), NA_character_,
              sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
  v <- sub("^0\\.",  ".",  v)
  v <- sub("^-0\\.", "-.", v)
  v
}

format_p <- function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("NA")
  if (p < 0.001) return("&lt; .001")
  s <- sprintf("%.3f", p)
  sub("^0", "", s)
}

fdr_stars <- function(p) {
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  if (p < 0.001) return(" \\*\\*\\*")
  if (p < 0.01)  return(" \\*\\*")
  if (p < 0.05)  return(" \\*")
  ""
}


xbar_colors <- function(x, cutoff,
                        x_lo = ctq_x_limits[1], x_hi = ctq_x_limits[2],
                        hw   = xbar_neutral_halfwidth) {
  ramp_lo <- grDevices::colorRamp(c(xbar_green,   xbar_neutral))  # low → neutral
  ramp_hi <- grDevices::colorRamp(c(xbar_neutral, xbar_orange))   # neutral → high
  to_hex  <- function(m) grDevices::rgb(m[1], m[2], m[3], maxColorValue = 255)
  clamp01 <- function(t) min(max(t, 0), 1)

  has_cut <- !is.null(cutoff) && is.finite(cutoff) &&
             cutoff > x_lo && cutoff < x_hi

  vapply(x, function(xi) {
    if (!has_cut) {
      t <- clamp01((xi - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo))
      return(to_hex(grDevices::colorRamp(c(xbar_green, xbar_orange))(t)))
    }

    lo_edge <- max(cutoff - hw, x_lo)   # left edge of the neutral plateau
    hi_edge <- min(cutoff + hw, x_hi)   # right edge of the neutral plateau

    if (xi <= lo_edge) {
      denom <- lo_edge - x_lo
      t <- if (denom > 0) clamp01((xi - x_lo) / denom) else 1
      to_hex(ramp_lo(t))
    } else if (xi >= hi_edge) {
      denom <- x_hi - hi_edge
      t <- if (denom > 0) clamp01((xi - hi_edge) / denom) else 0
      to_hex(ramp_hi(t))
    } else {
      xbar_neutral                       # neutral plateau around the cutoff
    }
  }, character(1))
}

make_xbar_plot <- function(cutoff, ctq_abbr, base_size = 11) {
  x_lo <- ctq_x_limits[1]
  x_hi <- ctq_x_limits[2]
  head_len <- (x_hi - x_lo) * xbar_arrow_frac   # arrowhead length (severity units)

  shaft_lo <- x_lo + head_len                   # left edge of the gradient shaft
  shaft_hi <- x_hi - head_len                   # right edge of the gradient shaft

  shaft_h <- 0.30   # half-height of the rectangular shaft (was 0.45)
  head_h  <- 0.67   # half-height of the (taller, now SMALLER) arrowheads (was 1.0)
  y_lim   <- 1.0    # plotting-window half-height (kept = old head_h so the panel

  n      <- 512
  xs     <- seq(shaft_lo, shaft_hi, length.out = n)
  bar_df <- data.frame(x = xs, fillcol = xbar_colors(xs, cutoff))
  tile_w <- (shaft_hi - shaft_lo) / (n - 1)

  left_head <- data.frame(
    x = c(x_lo, shaft_lo, shaft_lo),
    y = c(0,    head_h,   -head_h)
  )
  right_head <- data.frame(
    x = c(x_hi, shaft_hi, shaft_hi),
    y = c(0,    head_h,   -head_h)
  )
  left_col  <- xbar_colors(x_lo, cutoff)   # green tip (low severity)
  right_col <- xbar_colors(x_hi, cutoff)   # orange tip (high severity)

  jn_x_lbl <- paste0(ctq_abbr, " Severity")

  ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = left_head,  aes(x = x, y = y),
                 fill = left_col,  colour = NA) +
    geom_polygon(data = right_head, aes(x = x, y = y),
                 fill = right_col, colour = NA) +
    geom_tile(data = bar_df, aes(x = x, y = 0, fill = fillcol),
              width = tile_w, height = 2 * shaft_h) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = ctq_x_limits, breaks = ctq_x_breaks,
                       expand = ctq_x_expand) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-y_lim, y_lim),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0.08)) +
    labs(x = jn_x_lbl, y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = panel_font) +
    theme(
      text         = element_text(family = panel_font),
      axis.title.x = element_text(family = panel_font, size = AXIS_TITLE_SZ),
      axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
      axis.title.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.line.x  = element_blank(),
      axis.line.y  = element_blank(),
      plot.margin  = margin(0, 8, 4, 8)
    )
}

make_trajectory_plot <- function(M4, voi, y_label, ctq_var,
                                 ctq_label, ctq_abbr,
                                 raw_p = NA_real_, fdr_p = NA_real_,
                                 age_bounds = numeric(0),
                                 vline_bounds = NULL,
                                 sd_mult = 2,
                                 base_size = 11,
                                 effect = "interaction") {

  short_metric <- voi_subtitle[[voi]]
  voi_title_html <- sprintf(
    "%s Development for High and Low %s",
    short_metric, ctq_abbr
  )

  fdr_sig <- !is.na(fdr_p) && fdr_p < 0.05
  effect_lbl <- if (identical(effect, "baseline"))
    sprintf("%s main effect", ctq_abbr) else sprintf("Age &times; %s", ctq_abbr)
  pval_sub_html <- sprintf(
    "%s: <i>p</i> = %s; <i>FDR</i> = %s%s",
    effect_lbl, format_p(raw_p), format_p(fdr_p), fdr_stars(fdr_p)
  )
  pval_sub_color <- if (fdr_sig) "red" else "black"

  if (is.null(M4)) {
    return(ggplot() + theme_void() + labs(title = voi_title_html) +
             annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "Model failed",
                      family = panel_font, colour = "grey40"))
  }

  ctq_mean <- mean(data[[ctq_var]], na.rm = TRUE)
  ctq_sd   <- sd(  data[[ctq_var]], na.rm = TRUE)

  cov_means <- list(
    NonVerbal_Std_centered = 0,
    child_sex              = mean(data$child_sex, na.rm = TRUE),
    eprime                 = mean(data$eprime,    na.rm = TRUE)
  )

  age_c_range <- seq(min(data$age_centered, na.rm = TRUE),
                     max(data$age_centered, na.rm = TRUE),
                     length.out = 200)
  has_age   <- "age" %in% names(data)
  age_offset <- if (has_age)
    mean(data$age - data$age_centered, na.rm = TRUE) else 0

  vcov_M4  <- as.matrix(vcov(M4))
  fe_terms <- delete.response(terms(lme4::nobars(formula(M4))))

  build_pred <- function(level_key, ctq_val) {
    df <- data.frame(
      age_centered           = age_c_range,
      age_squared            = age_c_range^2,
      NonVerbal_Std_centered = cov_means$NonVerbal_Std_centered,
      child_sex              = cov_means$child_sex,
      eprime                 = cov_means$eprime,
      ctq_level              = level_key,
      stringsAsFactors       = FALSE
    )
    df[[ctq_var]] <- ctq_val
    df$predicted  <- tryCatch(predict(M4, newdata = df, re.form = NA),
                              error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, nrow(df)))
    ci_vals <- tryCatch({
      mm     <- model.matrix(fe_terms, data = df)
      shared <- intersect(colnames(mm), colnames(vcov_M4))
      se     <- sqrt(pmax(diag(mm[, shared] %*%
                               tcrossprod(vcov_M4[shared, shared],
                                          mm[, shared])), 0))
      list(lo = df$predicted - 1.96 * se,
           hi = df$predicted + 1.96 * se)
    }, error = function(e) list(lo = rep(NA_real_, nrow(df)),
                                hi = rep(NA_real_, nrow(df))))
    df$ci_lo <- ci_vals$lo
    df$ci_hi <- ci_vals$hi
    df
  }

  pred_high <- build_pred("plus_sd",  ctq_mean + sd_mult * ctq_sd)
  pred_low  <- build_pred("minus_sd", ctq_mean - sd_mult * ctq_sd)
  pred_high$age_x <- pred_high$age_centered + age_offset
  pred_low$age_x  <- pred_low$age_centered  + age_offset

  interp_at_x <- function(df, x_target) {
    x <- df$age_x
    if (x_target < min(x) || x_target > max(x)) return(NULL)
    i_lo <- max(which(x <= x_target))
    i_hi <- min(which(x >= x_target))
    if (i_lo == i_hi) return(df[i_lo, , drop = FALSE])
    frac <- (x_target - x[i_lo]) / (x[i_hi] - x[i_lo])
    row  <- df[i_lo, , drop = FALSE]
    for (col in c("predicted", "ci_lo", "ci_hi", "age_centered")) {
      row[[col]] <- df[[col]][i_lo] +
                    frac * (df[[col]][i_hi] - df[[col]][i_lo])
    }
    row$age_x <- x_target
    row
  }

  split_level <- function(df_level, age_bounds) {
    df_level <- df_level[order(df_level$age_x), ]
    xlo <- min(df_level$age_x); xhi <- max(df_level$age_x)

    if (length(age_bounds) < 2) {
      df_level$region     <- "sig"
      df_level$sub_region <- "sig_all"
      return(df_level)
    }

    b1 <- min(age_bounds); b2 <- max(age_bounds)

    if (b2 <= xlo || b1 >= xhi) {
      df_level$region     <- "sig"
      df_level$sub_region <- "sig_all"
      return(df_level)
    }

    c1 <- max(b1, xlo)   # left edge of the muted region within the panel
    c2 <- min(b2, xhi)   # right edge of the muted region within the panel

    pieces <- list()
    add_piece <- function(lo, hi, region, sub) {
      if (hi <= lo) return(invisible())
      inside <- df_level[df_level$age_x > lo & df_level$age_x < hi, ]
      pt_lo  <- interp_at_x(df_level, lo)
      pt_hi  <- interp_at_x(df_level, hi)
      seg    <- rbind(pt_lo, inside, pt_hi)
      if (is.null(seg) || nrow(seg) == 0) return(invisible())
      seg$region     <- region
      seg$sub_region <- sub
      pieces[[length(pieces) + 1]] <<- seg
    }

    if (b1 > xlo) add_piece(xlo, c1, "sig", "sig_low")
    add_piece(c1, c2, "nonsig", "nonsig")
    if (b2 < xhi) add_piece(c2, xhi, "sig", "sig_high")

    do.call(rbind, pieces)
  }

  pred_df <- rbind(
    split_level(pred_high, age_bounds),
    split_level(pred_low,  age_bounds)
  )

  col_map <- c(
    "sig.plus_sd"     = col_high_sig,    "sig.minus_sd"     = col_low_sig,
    "nonsig.plus_sd"  = col_high_nonsig, "nonsig.minus_sd"  = col_low_nonsig
  )
  pred_df$style_key <- paste(pred_df$region, pred_df$ctq_level, sep = ".")
  pred_df$group_key <- paste(pred_df$ctq_level, pred_df$sub_region, sep = ".")

  spag <- data[!is.na(data[[voi]]) & !is.na(data[[ctq_var]]), ]
  spag <- spag[order(spag$id, spag$age_centered), ]
  spag$age_x <- if (has_age) spag$age else spag$age_centered

  vline_pos <- if (!is.null(vline_bounds)) vline_bounds else age_bounds
  vlines <- if (length(vline_pos) >= 1) {
    geom_vline(xintercept = vline_pos, linetype = "dashed",
               colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4)
  } else NULL

  ggplot() +
    vlines +
    geom_line(data = spag,
              aes(x = age_x, y = .data[[voi]], group = id),
              colour = "gray60", alpha = 0.20, linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_ribbon(data = pred_df,
                aes(x = age_x, ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi,
                    group = group_key, fill = style_key),
                alpha = 0.25, colour = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(data = pred_df,
              aes(x = age_x, y = predicted,
                  group = group_key, colour = style_key, alpha = region),
              linewidth = 1.1, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = col_map, guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual( values = col_map, guide = "none") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("sig" = 1, "nonsig" = 0.3), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_x_breaks) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) strip_lead0(x, 2)) +
    labs(title    = voi_title_html,
         subtitle = pval_sub_html,
         x = "Age", y = y_label) +
    theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = panel_font) +
    theme(
      text         = element_text(family = panel_font),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.title   = ggtext::element_markdown(
                        face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                        family = panel_font, size = SUBPLOT_TITLE_SZ,
                        margin = margin(b = 6)),
      plot.subtitle = ggtext::element_markdown(
                        hjust = 0.5,
                        family = panel_font, size = SUBPLOT_SUB_SZ,
                        colour = pval_sub_color,
                        margin = margin(b = 4)),
      axis.title.x = element_text(family = panel_font, size = AXIS_TITLE_SZ),
      axis.title.y = ggtext::element_markdown(family = panel_font,
                                              size = Y_AXIS_TITLE_SZ),
      axis.text    = element_text(family = panel_font, size = AXIS_TEXT_SZ),
      plot.margin  = margin(6, 8, 14, 8)
    )
}

make_jn_plot <- function(jn_adv, ctq_var, ctq_label, ctq_abbr, cutoff,
                         voi, base_size = 11) {

  if (is.null(jn_adv) || is.null(jn_adv$cbands) || nrow(jn_adv$cbands) == 0) {
    return(ggplot() + theme_void() +
             annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "(J-N unavailable)",
                      family = panel_font, colour = "grey50", size = 3))
  }

  cb <- jn_adv$cbands

  modx_col <- names(cb)[1]
  est_col  <- grep("Slope|Est|estimate|fit", names(cb), value = TRUE)[1]
  lwr_col  <- grep("Lower|lower|lwr|LCL",    names(cb), value = TRUE)[1]
  upr_col  <- grep("Upper|upper|upr|UCL",    names(cb), value = TRUE)[1]

  bounds <- as.numeric(jn_adv$bounds)
  bounds <- bounds[is.finite(bounds)]
  bounds <- sort(bounds)

  has_nonsig <- length(bounds) >= 2
  b1 <- if (has_nonsig) bounds[1] else NA_real_
  b2 <- if (has_nonsig) bounds[length(bounds)] else NA_real_

  in_nonsig_at <- function(x) has_nonsig && x >= b1 && x <= b2

  interp_at <- function(df, x_target) {
    x <- df[[modx_col]]
    if (x_target < min(x) || x_target > max(x)) return(NULL)
    i_lo <- max(which(x <= x_target))
    i_hi <- min(which(x >= x_target))
    if (i_lo == i_hi) return(df[i_lo, , drop = FALSE])
    frac <- (x_target - x[i_lo]) / (x[i_hi] - x[i_lo])
    row  <- df[i_lo, , drop = FALSE]
    for (col in c(est_col, lwr_col, upr_col)) {
      row[[col]] <- df[[col]][i_lo] +
                    frac * (df[[col]][i_hi] - df[[col]][i_lo])
    }
    row[[modx_col]] <- x_target
    row
  }

  slope_at <- function(x) {
    r <- interp_at(cb, x)
    if (is.null(r)) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(r[[est_col]])
  }
  color_at <- function(x) {
    if (in_nonsig_at(x)) return(jn_col_nonsig)        # grey — non-significant
    s <- slope_at(x)
    if (!is.na(s) && s < 0) return(jn_col_high_sig)   # red  — sig negative slope
    jn_col_low_sig                                     # blue — sig positive slope
  }

  x_min <- min(cb[[modx_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  x_max <- max(cb[[modx_col]], na.rm = TRUE)
  splits <- c(if (!is.null(cutoff) && is.finite(cutoff)) cutoff else NULL,
              if (has_nonsig) bounds else NULL)
  splits <- sort(unique(splits[splits > x_min & splits < x_max]))
  endpoints <- c(x_min, splits, x_max)

  segments <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(length(endpoints) - 1)) {
    xL <- endpoints[i]; xR <- endpoints[i + 1]
    seg_col <- color_at((xL + xR) / 2)
    inside  <- cb[cb[[modx_col]] > xL & cb[[modx_col]] < xR, ]
    pt_L    <- interp_at(cb, xL)
    pt_R    <- interp_at(cb, xR)
    seg     <- rbind(pt_L, inside, pt_R)
    if (nrow(seg) == 0) next
    seg$seg_id    <- i
    seg$color_key <- seg_col
    segments[[length(segments) + 1]] <- seg
  }
  seg_df <- do.call(rbind, segments)

  col_map <- c(jn_col_low_sig, jn_col_nonsig, jn_col_high_sig)
  names(col_map) <- col_map

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_ribbon(data = seg_df,
                aes(x = .data[[modx_col]],
                    ymin = .data[[lwr_col]],
                    ymax = .data[[upr_col]],
                    group = seg_id, fill = color_key),
                alpha = 0.30, colour = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_line(data = seg_df,
              aes(x = .data[[modx_col]], y = .data[[est_col]],
                  group = seg_id, colour = color_key),
              linewidth = 0.9, na.rm = TRUE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = col_map, guide = "none") +
    scale_fill_manual( values = col_map, guide = "none")

  p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
                      colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4)
  if (has_nonsig) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = bounds, linetype = "dashed",
                        colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.4)
  }
  if (!is.null(cutoff) && is.finite(cutoff)) {
    p <- p + geom_vline(xintercept = cutoff, linetype = "solid",
                        colour = col_cutoff, linewidth = 0.4)
  }

  short_metric <- voi_subtitle[[voi]]
  jn_title <- sprintf(
    "Significant %s &nbsp;Development<br>across %s Severity",
    short_metric, ctq_abbr
  )
  jn_y_lbl <- paste0("Age-Related Slope<br>of ", short_metric)

  p +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = ctq_x_limits, breaks = ctq_x_breaks,
                       expand = ctq_x_expand) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 4),
      labels = function(x) strip_lead0(x, 2)
    ) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = jn_y_lbl, title = jn_title) +
    theme_classic(base_size = base_size, base_family = panel_font) +
    theme(
      text         = element_text(family = panel_font),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.title   = ggtext::element_markdown(
                        face = "bold", hjust = 0.5,
                        family = panel_font, size = SUBPLOT_TITLE_SZ,
                        lineheight = 1.35,
                        margin = margin(t = 0, b = 10)),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(family = panel_font, size = AXIS_TEXT_SZ,
                                  colour = "black"),
      axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.3),
      axis.line.x  = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
      axis.title.y = ggtext::element_markdown(family = panel_font,
                                              size = Y_AXIS_TITLE_SZ,
                                              lineheight = 1.1),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(family = panel_font, size = AXIS_TEXT_SZ),
      plot.margin  = margin(6, 8, 2, 8)
    )
}


# Johnson-Neyman analysis of the age slope across levels of the CTQ score
# (the CTQ score is the "moderator"). Returns the interactions-package result.
run_jn <- function(model, pred_name, modx_name, alpha = 0.05) {
  tryCatch(suppressWarnings(eval(bquote(
    interactions::johnson_neyman(.(model), pred = .(as.name(pred_name)), modx = .(as.name(modx_name)),
                                 alpha = .(alpha), plot = FALSE)))), error = function(e) NULL)
}

# Small legends (colored squares with labels), shown in a strip above the figure
make_line_legend <- function(items, label_size = 2.5, line_lh = 1.0, swatch_size = 3.5) {
  n  <- length(items); ys <- seq(n, 1)
  df_pt  <- data.frame(x = 0.18, y = ys, col = vapply(items, `[[`, character(1), "color"))
  df_txt <- data.frame(x = 0.40, y = ys, label = vapply(items, `[[`, character(1), "label"))
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(data = df_pt, aes(x = x, y = y, colour = col), shape = 15, size = swatch_size) +
    scale_colour_identity() +
    ggtext::geom_richtext(data = df_txt, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label), hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5,
                          family = panel_font, size = label_size, lineheight = line_lh,
                          fill = NA, label.colour = NA, label.padding = unit(0, "pt")) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 2.0)) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0.5, n + 0.5)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + theme_void() +
    theme(text = element_text(family = panel_font), plot.margin = margin(4, 6, 4, 6))
}
legend_traj <- make_line_legend(list(list(color = col_low_sig, label = "low adversity"),
                                     list(color = col_high_sig, label = "high adversity")))
legend_jn   <- make_line_legend(list(list(color = jn_col_low_sig, label = "sig. positive<br>development"),
                                     list(color = jn_col_high_sig, label = "sig. negative<br>development")),
                                line_lh = 1.1)

# One complete panel: title + trajectory plot + Johnson-Neyman plot + arrow
img_w <- 4; img_h <- 5.55                 # size (inches) of one panel in the paper's figure
make_figure_panel <- function(k, voi) {
  ctq_raw   <- predictors[k, "raw"]       # raw CTQ score (so J-N and axes are on the CTQ-score scale)
  ctq_label <- predictors[k, "name"]; ctq_abbr <- predictors[k, "abbr"]
  # Model 4 with the raw CTQ score (otherwise identical to the model used in the tables)
  quad <- fits[[k]][[voi]]$use_quadratic
  f4 <- if (quad) paste(voi, "~ age_centered *", ctq_raw, "+ age_squared *", ctq_raw, "+", covariates, "+", random_fx)
        else      paste(voi, "~ age_centered *", ctq_raw, "+", covariates, "+", random_fx)
  M4 <- fit_lmm(f4, dat)$model
  raw_p <- fixed_effects(M4); raw_p <- raw_p$p[raw_p$term == paste0("age_centered:", ctq_raw)]
  fdr_p <- fdr[[k]]["age", voi]
  p_traj <- make_trajectory_plot(M4 = M4, voi = voi, y_label = panel_y_labels[[voi]], ctq_var = ctq_raw,
                                 ctq_label = ctq_label, ctq_abbr = ctq_abbr, raw_p = raw_p, fdr_p = fdr_p,
                                 age_bounds = numeric(0), vline_bounds = NULL, sd_mult = 1, base_size = 11)
  p_jn  <- make_jn_plot(jn_adv = run_jn(M4, "age_centered", ctq_raw), ctq_var = ctq_raw, ctq_label = ctq_label,
                        ctq_abbr = ctq_abbr, cutoff = cutoffs[[k]], voi = voi, base_size = 11)
  p_bar <- make_xbar_plot(cutoff = cutoffs[[k]], ctq_abbr = ctq_abbr, base_size = 11)
  metric_symbol <- if (grepl("LastBlock", voi)) "last block" else voi_subtitle[[voi]]
  title_html <- sprintf("Effect of %s (%s)<br>on %s (%s)", ctq_label, ctq_abbr, voi_full_name[[voi]], metric_symbol)
  title_theme <- theme(plot.title = ggtext::element_markdown(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, family = panel_font,
                                                              size = TITLE_SZ, lineheight = 1.35, margin = margin(b = 14)))
  p_traj / p_jn / p_bar + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1, 0.20)) +
    plot_annotation(title = title_html, theme = title_theme)
}
# Moderate-severity CTQ cutoffs (Bernstein & Fink, 1998)
cutoffs <- c(EA = 13, PA = 10, SA = 8, EN = 15, PN = 10)
```

## Supplemental Table 5. Baseline correlations among the CTQ adversity predictors, covariates, and learning metrics

Pearson correlations at baseline (T1; n = 166). Stars mark uncorrected p-values (* p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001). Sex is coded 0 = male, 1 = female.

```{r corr-functions}
# Pearson correlation between two variables, formatted ".65***"
cor_cell <- function(x, y) {
  ok <- complete.cases(x, y)
  ct <- cor.test(x[ok], y[ok])
  paste0(f2(unname(ct$estimate)), stars(ct$p.value))
}
# Correlation table: rows and columns are named vectors (variable name = label).
# lower_only = TRUE shows only the lower triangle (for a variable with itself).
cor_table <- function(rows, cols, lower_only = FALSE) {
  m <- matrix("", length(rows), length(cols), dimnames = list(unname(rows), unname(cols)))
  for (i in seq_along(rows)) for (j in seq_along(cols)) {
    if (lower_only && j >= i) { m[i, j] <- if (i == j) "—" else ""; next }
    m[i, j] <- cor_cell(t1[[names(rows)[i]]], t1[[names(cols)[j]]])
  }
  out <- data.frame(Variable = rownames(m), m, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  out
}

Age² is shown only where the quadratic model was retained (likelihood-ratio test, p < .05). FDR correction is across the eight primary metrics (Age: eight linear tests; Age²: eight curvature tests); deck-level models are uncorrected.

```{r supp-table8}

                 deckC_proportion = "Deck C: good, frequent losses", deckD_proportion = "Deck D: good, infrequent losses",
                 good_proportion_LastBlock = "Good Deck Proportion", bad_proportion_LastBlock = "Bad Deck Proportion",
                 net_good_bad_LastBlock = "Net Performance",

                 betaB = "Go Bias (βb)", Arew_qnormed = "Reward Learning Rate (Arew)",
                 Apun_qnormed = "Punishment Learning Rate (Apun)",
                 Overall_A = "Averaged Single Learning Rate ((Arew + Apun)/2)", betaF = "Win/Loss Frequency Sensitivity (βf)")
gs8 <- lapply(setNames(names(t8_outcomes), names(t8_outcomes)), function(y) growth_shape(y, dat))
# p-value of the age^2 term from the quadratic model, for every outcome (for FDR)
p_quad <- sapply(gs8, function(g) summary(g$r2$model)$coefficients["age_squared", "Pr(>|t|)"])
p_age  <- sapply(gs8, function(g) {
  m <- if (g$use_quadratic) g$r2$model else g$r1$model
  summary(m)$coefficients["age_centered", "Pr(>|t|)"]
})
# FDR families: (last-block traditional + model-based) and (full-task traditional + model-based)
rl <- names(outcomes)[4:8]
fam_last <- c(names(outcomes)[1:3], rl)
fam_full <- c(names(fulltask_outcomes), rl)
# Adjusted p-values: first within the last-block family, then replace the three
# traditional metrics by their full-task versions (the model-based metrics keep
# their last-block-family values, as in the paper's table).
q_age <- q_quad <- setNames(rep(NA_real_, length(gs8)), names(gs8))
q_age[fam_last]  <- p.adjust(p_age[fam_last], "BH");  q_quad[fam_last] <- p.adjust(p_quad[fam_last], "BH")
qa_full <- p.adjust(p_age[fam_full], "BH");           qq_full <- p.adjust(p_quad[fam_full], "BH")
q_age[names(fulltask_outcomes)]  <- qa_full[names(fulltask_outcomes)]
q_quad[names(fulltask_outcomes)] <- qq_full[names(fulltask_outcomes)]

fmt_row <- function(y, term) {
  g  <- gs8[[y]]
  m  <- if (g$use_quadratic) g$r2$model else g$r1$model
  tm <- if (term == "Age") "age_centered" else "age_squared"
  if (!tm %in% rownames(summary(m)$coefficients)) return(NULL)
  fe <- fixed_effects(m); r <- fe[fe$term == tm, ]
  q  <- if (y %in% names(t8_outcomes)[1:4]) "—" else fp(if (term == "Age") q_age[y] else q_quad[y])
  c(t8_outcomes[[y]], term, f3(r$est), sprintf("[%s – %s]", f3(r$lo), f3(r$hi)), fp(r$p), q)
}

## Supplemental Table 9. Full nested model results

Models 1-4 for each learning metric and each CTQ predictor (56 sub-tables, 9.1-9.56). Model 1 = unconditional linear growth; Model 2 = unconditional quadratic growth; Model 3 = winning growth shape plus covariates (nonverbal IQ, sex, administration mode); Model 4 = Model 3 plus the CTQ predictor and its interaction with age (and age² if the quadratic shape won). Cells show unstandardized b, uncorrected significance stars (* p < .05, ** p < .01, *** p < .001), and the 95% CI. A "—" in the τ₁₁ row means the random age slope was dropped because the fit was singular. J-N = Johnson-Neyman: CTQ scores (raw scale) at which the age slope is significant, shown for age interactions with p < .05.

```{r table9-function}
# Builds one Supplemental Table 9 sub-table: the Model 1-4 results for one CTQ
# predictor (pred_key, e.g. "EA") and one learning metric (outcome).
show_table9 <- function(pred_key, outcome) {
  f   <- fits[[pred_key]][[outcome]]
  P   <- predictors[pred_key, ]
  cv  <- P$centered
  mods <- list(f$M1, f$M2, f$M3, f$M4)
  slope_dropped <- f$slope_dropped
  fes <- lapply(mods, fixed_effects)
  dash <- "—"

  # Cell for a fixed effect (est, stars, CI), or "—" if the term is not in the model
  fe_cell <- function(i, term) {
    r <- fes[[i]][fes[[i]]$term == term, ]
    if (nrow(r) == 0) return(dash)
    s <- stars(r$p)
    sprintf("%s%s\n[%s – %s]", f3(r$est), ifelse(s == "", "", paste0(" ", s)), f3(r$lo), f3(r$hi))
  }
  # Rows of fixed effects: label and term name
  terms <- list(c("Constant", "(Intercept)"), c("Age", "age_centered"), c("Age²", "age_squared"),
                c("K-BIT Nonverbal Standard IQ", "NonVerbal_Std_centered"), c("Child Sex", "child_sex"),
                c("On-site Administration", "eprime"),
                c(paste(P$abbr, "Baseline Effect"), ctq_terms(cv)[["baseline"]]),
                c(paste("Age ×", P$name), ctq_terms(cv)[["age"]]))
  rows <- list()
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("<b>Fixed Effects</b>", "", "", "", "")
  for (t in terms) {
    rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c(t[1], sapply(1:4, function(i) fe_cell(i, t[2])))
    # Johnson-Neyman row under the age interaction when it is significant (p < .05)
    if (t[2] == ctq_terms(cv)[["age"]] && term_p(f, "age") < .05) {
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("J-N Adversity Levels of Sig", dash, dash, dash, jn_text(f$M4, cv))
    }
  }
  if (f$use_quadratic) rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c(paste("Age² ×", P$name), dash, dash, dash, fe_cell(4, ctq_terms(cv)[["age2"]]))

  # Random effects
  res <- Map(function(m, sd) random_effects(m, sd), mods, slope_dropped)
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("<b>Random Effects</b>", "", "", "", "")
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("σ²", sapply(res, function(r) sprintf("%.2f", r$sigma2)))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("τ₀₀ (id)", sapply(res, function(r) sprintf("%.2f", r$tau00)))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("τ₁₁ (id.age)", mapply(function(r, sd) if (sd) dash else sprintf("%.2f", r$tau11), res, slope_dropped))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("N (id)", rep(as.character(ngrps(f$M4)[["id"]]), 4))

  # Fit statistics
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("<b>Fit Statistics</b>", "", "", "", "")
  ll <- sapply(mods, function(m) as.numeric(logLik(m)))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("AIC", sprintf("%.1f", sapply(mods, AIC)))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("BIC", sprintf("%.1f", sapply(mods, BIC)))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("Log-Likelihood", sprintf("%.1f", ll))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("Deviance", sprintf("%.1f", -2 * ll))

  # Model comparisons (likelihood-ratio tests)
  lrt_text <- function(a) sprintf("χ²(%d) = %.2f%s", a$Df[2], a$Chisq[2], ifelse(stars(a$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]) == "", "", paste0(" ", stars(a$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2]))))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("<b>Model Comparisons</b>", "", "", "", "")
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("Compared to Model 1", "", lrt_text(f$lrt_12),
                                if (!f$use_quadratic) lrt_text(f$lrt_ref3) else "",
                                if (!f$use_quadratic) lrt_text(f$lrt_ref4) else "")
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("Compared to Model 2", "", "", if (f$use_quadratic) lrt_text(f$lrt_ref3) else "",
                                if (f$use_quadratic) lrt_text(f$lrt_ref4) else "")
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("Compared to Model 3", "", "", "", lrt_text(f$lrt_34))

  # Intraclass correlation and R-squared
  rr <- lapply(mods, r2)
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("ICC", sprintf("%.2f", sapply(mods, icc)))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("Conditional R²", sprintf("%.2f", sapply(rr, function(x) x["R2c"])))
  rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- c("Marginal R²",    sprintf("%.2f", sapply(rr, function(x) x["R2m"])))

  tab <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, rows), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(tab) <- c("", "Model 1", "Model 2", "Model 3", "Model 4")
  show_table(tab)
}
```

## Supplemental Table 12. Specificity analyses for the three adversity effects of interest

For the three effects that survive FDR correction, Model 4 was re-estimated with all other CTQ subscales (and their interactions with age) entered simultaneously. The CTQ × age interaction from the original Model 4 (each subscale alone) is shown next to the same interaction when all five subscales are in the model. p-values are uncorrected.

```{r sens-fits}
# The three effects of interest (CTQ subscale, outcome)
effects <- list(
  list(k = "EA", y = "Apun_qnormed",              label = "Emotional Abuse × Age on Punishment Learning Rate (Apun)"),
  list(k = "PA", y = "betaB",                     label = "Physical Abuse × Age on Go Bias (βb)"),
  list(k = "PA", y = "good_proportion_LastBlock", label = "Physical Abuse × Age on Good Deck Proportion (last block)"))

# Extra covariates: the other four subscales and their interactions with age
other_subscales_terms <- function(k) {
  others <- setdiff(predictors[subscales, "centered"], predictors[k, "centered"])
  paste("+", paste(c(others, paste0("age_centered:", others)), collapse = " + "))
}
# Minimization/Denial scale and its interaction with age; only participants with
# a Minimization/Denial score are included (centered versions: *_mdr_c)
dat_mdr <- dat[!is.na(dat$ctq_mdr_T1_mdr_c), ]
mdr_terms <- "+ ctq_mdr_T1_mdr_c + age_centered:ctq_mdr_T1_mdr_c"

sens <- lapply(effects, function(e) {
  cv <- predictors[e$k, "centered"]
  list(orig = fits[[e$k]][[e$y]],
       oth  = fit_models(e$y, cv, dat, extra_terms = other_subscales_terms(e$k)),
       mdr  = fit_models(e$y, sub("_T1_c$", "_T1_mdr_c", cv), dat_mdr, extra_terms = mdr_terms))
})
# estimate [CI] and p-value of the age x CTQ interaction in a fit
age_effect <- function(fit) {
  fe <- fixed_effects(fit$M4)
  r <- fe[fe$term == ctq_terms(fit$ctq_var)[["age"]], ]
  c(cell_est_ci(r$est, r$lo, r$hi, NA), fp(r$p))
}
```

```{r supp-table12}
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(effects), function(i) c(effects[[i]]$label, age_effect(sens[[i]]$orig), age_effect(sens[[i]]$oth))))
tab <- as.data.frame(tab, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(tab) <- c("Adversity × Age effect", "Model 4 (each CTQ predictor alone): b [95% CI]", "p-value",
                "Model 4 with all five CTQ subscales: b [95% CI]", "p-value ")
show_table(tab)
```

## Supplemental Table 14. Assumption checks for the three adversity effects of interest

Normality and constant variance of the Model 4 residuals: skewness and excess kurtosis of the standardized residuals, the percentage of residuals beyond ±2 and ±3 SD (about 4.6% and 0.3% are expected under normality), and Spearman correlations between the absolute residuals and the fitted values and age.

```{r supp-table14}
# The Model 4 fits for the three effects (already fit above)
focal <- lapply(effects, function(e) fits[[e$k]][[e$y]])
skew   <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^3) / mean((x - mean(x))^2)^1.5
exkurt <- function(x) mean((x - mean(x))^4) / mean((x - mean(x))^2)^2 - 3
age_offset <- mean(dat$age - dat$age_centered)
resid_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(focal), function(i) {
  m <- focal[[i]]$M4
  data.frame(model = effects[[i]]$label, fitted = fitted(m), resid = resid(m),
             z = resid(m) / sigma(m),                       # standardized residual
             age = m@frame$age_centered + age_offset)
}))
resid_df$model <- factor(resid_df$model, levels = sapply(effects, `[[`, "label"))
rho <- function(a, b) cor(a, b, method = "spearman")
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(levels(resid_df$model), function(nm) {
  d <- resid_df[resid_df$model == nm, ]
  c(nm, f2(skew(d$z)), f2(exkurt(d$z)), sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(abs(d$z) > 2)), sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(abs(d$z) > 3)),
    f2(rho(abs(d$resid), d$fitted)), f2(rho(abs(d$resid), d$age)))
}))
tab <- as.data.frame(tab, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(tab) <- c("Adversity × Age effect", "Skewness", "Excess kurtosis", "% beyond ±2 SD", "% beyond ±3 SD",
                "ρ (|residual|, fitted values)", "ρ (|residual|, age)")
show_table(tab)
```

## Supplemental Figure 3. Residual diagnostics for the three adversity effects of interest

Left: normal Q-Q plots of the standardized residuals (points near the red line = approximately normal). Right: standardized residuals against fitted values (an even band around the red zero line with a flat blue smoother = constant variance).

```{r supp-figure3, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 9}
p_qq <- ggplot(resid_df, aes(sample = z)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = .35, size = 1) + stat_qq_line(colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical normal quantiles", y = "Standardized residuals", title = "Normal Q-Q plot") +

p_rf <- ggplot(resid_df, aes(fitted, z)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .35, size = 1) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, colour = "steelblue", linewidth = .8) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +

```

## Supplemental Table 15. Influence analyses for the three adversity effects of interest

The final Model 4 for each effect was re-estimated (a) leaving out each participant in turn (166 refits per effect; Table 15.1) and (b) after removing five participants at a time (Table 15.2). All p-values are uncorrected. The refits below take a few minutes.

```{r influence-fits}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Leave-one-participant-out refits. For every participant, all of their waves are
# removed and Model 4 is re-estimated. We save the age x CTQ estimate and p-value,
# plus two influence measures:
#   Cook's D  = how far ALL fixed-effect estimates move when the participant is removed
#   DFBETAS   = how far the key age x CTQ coefficient moves (in standard-error units;
#               positive = removing the participant lowers the estimate)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
ctrl <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
loo_one <- function(m, key, V, beta_full, id_drop) {
  sub <- dat[as.character(dat$id) != id_drop, ]
  m2 <- tryCatch(lmer(formula(m), data = sub, REML = FALSE, control = ctrl), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(m2)) return(NULL)
  dB <- beta_full - fixef(m2)[names(beta_full)]
  cf <- summary(m2)$coefficients[key, ]
  data.frame(id = id_drop,
             cook = drop(t(dB) %*% solve(V, dB)) / length(beta_full),
             dfbetas = unname(dB[key] / sqrt(V[key, key])),
             est = unname(cf["Estimate"]), p = unname(cf["Pr(>|t|)"]))
}
loo <- lapply(seq_along(effects), function(i) {
  m <- focal[[i]]$M4
  key <- ctq_terms(focal[[i]]$ctq_var)[["age"]]
  ids <- unique(as.character(getME(m, "flist")$id))
  do.call(rbind, mclapply(ids, function(j) loo_one(m, key, as.matrix(vcov(m)), fixef(m), j), mc.cores = n_cores))
})
```

### Supplemental Table 15.1. Leave-one-participant-out analysis

```{r supp-table15-1}
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(effects), function(i) {
  L <- loo[[i]]; m <- focal[[i]]$M4
  key <- ctq_terms(focal[[i]]$ctq_var)[["age"]]
  full <- summary(m)$coefficients[key, "Estimate"]
  c(effects[[i]]$label, f3(full), sprintf("%s to %s", f3(min(L$est)), f3(max(L$est))),
    ifelse(all(sign(L$est) == sign(full)), "Yes", "No"),
    sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * mean(L$p < .05)), fp(max(L$p)),
    sum(L$cook > 4 / nrow(L)), f3(max(L$cook)), f2(max(abs(L$dfbetas))))
}))
tab <- as.data.frame(tab, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(tab) <- c("Adversity × Age effect", "b, full sample", sprintf("Range of b across %d refits", nrow(loo[[1]])),
                "Same direction in all refits", "Refits with p < .05", "Largest p across refits",
                "Participants above Cook's D threshold (4/N)", "Largest Cook's D", "Largest |DFBETAS|")
show_table(tab)
```

### Supplemental Table 15.2. Re-estimation after removing influential or extreme participants

```{r supp-table15-2}
n_drop <- 5
tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(effects), function(i) {
  L <- loo[[i]]; m <- focal[[i]]$M4; ctq <- focal[[i]]$ctq_var
  key <- ctq_terms(ctq)[["age"]]
  # Participants to remove in each scenario
  top_cook <- L$id[order(-L$cook)][1:n_drop]                    # five largest Cook's D
  top_dfb  <- L$id[order(-abs(L$dfbetas))][1:n_drop]            # five largest |DFBETAS|
  person   <- aggregate(dat[[ctq]], list(id = dat$id), function(v) v[!is.na(v)][1])
  top_ctq  <- as.character(person$id[person$x >= sort(person$x, decreasing = TRUE)[n_drop]])  # highest CTQ scores
  scen <- list(character(0), top_cook, top_dfb, top_ctq)
  names(scen) <- c("None (full sample)",
                   "Drop the 5 most influential participants (Cook's D)",
                   "Drop the 5 most influential for this interaction (DFBETAS)",
                   sprintf("Drop the 5 participants with the highest %s scores", tolower(predictors[effects[[i]]$k, "name"])))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(scen), function(s) {
    keep <- dat[!(as.character(dat$id) %in% scen[[s]]), ]
    m2 <- lmer(formula(m), data = keep, REML = FALSE, control = ctrl)
    cf <- summary(m2)$coefficients[key, ]
    c(if (s == 1) effects[[i]]$label else "", names(scen)[s], length(unique(keep$id[!is.na(keep[[ctq]])])),
      f3(cf["Estimate"]), f3(cf["Std. Error"]), fp(cf["Pr(>|t|)"]))
  }))
}))
tab <- as.data.frame(tab, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(tab) <- c("Adversity × Age effect", "Participants removed", "N remaining", "b", "SE", "p-value")
show_table(tab)
```

## Supplemental Table 16. Expected change in Net Performance through the learning parameters, by adversity subtype

Model-based estimate of how abuse-related differences in learning could affect Net Performance. For youth 1 SD above and 1 SD below the mean baseline subscale score, the Model 4 growth models predict each learning parameter at each age (9-17 years). The predicted difference in each parameter (in SD units) is multiplied by that parameter's coefficient from the model with all four parameters together (Supplemental Table 7) and the four products are summed (Total). 95% intervals and p-values are Monte Carlo estimates (10,000 draws). The table shows the slope per year of age [95% CI] of the expected difference in Net Performance (percentage points). Values are model-based extrapolations.

```{r supp-table16}
set.seed(20261019)      # Monte Carlo draws below are random; the seed makes them reproducible
n_mc    <- 10000
AGE_REF <- 10.99        # age used to center age (mean age at baseline)
d16     <- d7           # data from Supplemental Table 7 (Net Performance in percentage points; standardized parameters)
pred_vars  <- c(EA = "ctq_EA_T1_c", PA = "ctq_PA_T1_c")
pred_names <- c(EA = "Emotional Abuse", PA = "Physical Abuse")
RS <- random_fx

# Model 4 for each parameter (same model as in the main analysis; this version
# writes the formula in the order used when these estimates were first computed)
fit_param_m4 <- function(y, p, data) {
  m_lin  <- fit_lmm(sprintf("%s ~ age_centered + %s + %s*age_centered + %s", y, covariates, p, RS), data)$model
  m_quad <- fit_lmm(sprintf("%s ~ age_centered + age_squared + %s + %s*age_centered + %s*age_squared + %s", y, covariates, p, p, RS), data)$model
  u1 <- fit_lmm(sprintf("%s ~ age_centered + %s", y, RS), data)$model
  u2 <- fit_lmm(sprintf("%s ~ age_centered + age_squared + %s", y, RS), data)$model
  quad <- tryCatch(anova(u1, u2)$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2] < .05, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (quad) m_quad else m_lin
}
par_fits <- lapply(pred_vars, function(p) { r <- lapply(names(params), function(v) fit_param_m4(v, p, dat)); names(r) <- names(params); r })

design <- function(m, nd) model.matrix(delete.response(terms(lme4::nobars(formula(m)))), nd)
sd_par <- sapply(names(params), function(v) sd(dat[[v]], na.rm = TRUE))
T1 <- dat$time == "T1"
# Mean -/+ 1 SD of the baseline subscale score
qsd <- lapply(pred_vars, function(p) mean(dat[[p]][T1], na.rm = TRUE) + c(-1, 1) * sd(dat[[p]][T1], na.rm = TRUE))
age_obs  <- range(dat$age, na.rm = TRUE)
age_grid <- seq(9, 17.25, by = 0.25); age_grid <- age_grid[age_grid >= age_obs[1] - 0.1 & age_grid <= age_obs[2]]

# Monte Carlo draws: (1) coefficients of the "all four parameters together" model
# for Net Performance, (2) coefficients of each parameter's Model 4
bd_joint <- mvrnorm(n_mc, fixef(m_together)[z_names], as.matrix(vcov(m_together))[z_names, z_names])
bpar_all <- lapply(names(pred_vars), function(k) {
  r <- lapply(names(params), function(v) { m <- par_fits[[k]][[v]]; mvrnorm(n_mc, fixef(m), as.matrix(vcov(m))) })
  names(r) <- names(params); r
}); names(bpar_all) <- names(pred_vars)

# At each age: predicted difference in each parameter between +1 SD and -1 SD
# youth (in parameter SD units), times the parameter's effect on Net Performance
ind <- list()
for (k in names(pred_vars)) {
  p <- pred_vars[[k]]
  for (a in age_grid) {
    contrib <- sapply(names(params), function(v) {
      m <- par_fits[[k]][[v]]
      nd <- data.frame(age_centered = a - AGE_REF, age_squared = (a - AGE_REF)^2, NonVerbal_Std_centered = 0,
                       child_sex = mean(dat$child_sex[T1]), eprime = 1)
      lo <- nd; hi <- nd; lo[[p]] <- qsd[[k]][1]; hi[[p]] <- qsd[[k]][2]
      dpar <- as.numeric(bpar_all[[k]][[v]] %*% t(design(m, hi) - design(m, lo)))
      dpar / sd_par[[v]] * bd_joint[, paste0(v, "_z")]
    })
    ind[[paste(k, a)]] <- list(k = k, a = a, contrib = contrib, tot = rowSums(contrib))
  }
}
# Slope over age of the expected difference (percentage points per year)
slope_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(pred_vars), function(k) {
  z  <- ind[paste(k, age_grid)]; ac <- age_grid - mean(age_grid)
  one <- function(getter, label, first) {
    M  <- sapply(z, getter)
    sl <- as.numeric(M %*% ac) / sum(ac^2)
    ci <- quantile(sl, c(.025, .975))
    c(if (first) pred_names[[k]] else "", label, sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", mean(sl), ci[1], ci[2]),
      fp(min(1, 2 * min(mean(sl > 0), mean(sl < 0)))))
  }
  rbind(one(function(x) x$tot, "Total (all four learning parameters)", TRUE),
        do.call(rbind, lapply(names(params), function(v) one(function(x) x$contrib[, v], params[[v]], FALSE))))
}))
tab <- as.data.frame(slope_rows, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(tab) <- c("Adversity Subtype", "Learning Predictor", "Slope per year [95% CI]", "Monte Carlo p-value")
show_table(tab)
```
